clue.text: Tone down article on painting

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to temper something is to moderate or soften it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Advice to soften the tone of a newspaper piece about a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a type of painting using pigment bound in egg yolk.

clue.text: Two kinds of flax used in rope-making

definitions.text: Two kinds of flax used in rope-making

parts.note: tow is the coarse short fibre of flax
line is the long fine fibre of flax

explanation.surface: A ropemaker uses two grades of flax fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope for hauling or pulling a vessel, made from flax fibres.

clue.text: Timekeeper ran into no more trouble

parts.note: to meet is to run into someone

indicators.note: trouble suggests these letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A timekeeper encountered no further problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome is a device that keeps musical time with regular ticks.

clue.text: High cost of providing closed-circuit link ?

definitions.meaning: a very high price is said to cost the world
a ground wire connecting an electrical circuit to the planet's surface

explanation.surface: Providing a link for closed-circuit TV costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It cost the earth' means it was ruinously expensive; electricians connect a circuit to the ground by a wire of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical ground connection completes a circuit, and something ruinously dear 'costs the earth'.

clue.text: Withdraws works of art

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means takes out or removes

explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to take away, and non-figurative paintings are also so called.

clue.text: The engraving Mrs Henry omitted

parts.note: Mrs Henry Wood was the Victorian novelist who wrote East Lynne
something cut has been left out or omitted

explanation.surface: An editor notes that a certain illustration was dropped from Mrs Henry's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Henry Wood was the Victorian author of the novel East Lynne, always billed under her husband's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print or engraving made from a carved block of timber.

clue.text: Caucasian naturalist ?

definitions.meaning: a Caucasian is a person of fair-skinned race
Gilbert ... was the eighteenth-century naturalist of Selborne

explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert White wrote The Natural History of Selborne, a classic of English nature writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale-skinned people are described by this colour, and Gilbert White was a famous English naturalist.

clue.text: Silly codger struck by railway engine

definitions.meaning: a buffer at the end of a line is hit by a train, especially an elderly one

explanation.surface: A doddering old man was hit by a train.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'old buffer' is a mildly mocking term for a fusty elderly man; buffers stop trains at the end of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuddy-duddy elderly man is so called, and an aged railway stop-block is struck by trains.

clue.text: Desire surgeon to support the firm

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a firm
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A wish for a doctor to back the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire, especially something belonging to another.

clue.text: Ground for reversal of old judgment in the end

indicators.note: reversal of means the word for the judgment is read backwards

parts.note: an arret is an old word for a judgment or decree of a court

explanation.surface: A case for overturning an old court decision in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground for' suggests legal grounds, but Ground is the definition. 'reversal of' turns ARRET into TERRA, the Latin for land.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features.

clue.text: Gem's liquid quality

parts.note: a jewel's clarity is graded by its lustre, as in 'of the first' grade, and the same word names the commonest liquid

explanation.surface: A jeweller admires the clear, liquid sparkle of a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarity of a diamond is called its water, and water is also the everyday liquid.

clue.text: He makes one-man submarine expeditions

parts.note: the 'submarine' is not a vessel but undersea, and the 'one-man' trip is a swimmer going down alone with mask or aqualung

explanation.definitionFit: A diver who goes beneath the sea under his own power, not in a boat, makes undersea trips alone.

clue.text: Old engine with metal mount

parts.note: iron is a metal
a horse is a mount for a rider

explanation.surface: An antique engine fitted out with a steel steed.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse was a nickname for the steam locomotive in its early days.

clue.text: Last month artist is revealed as extremist

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old commercial letters
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter was exposed a few weeks ago as a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ult.' (ultimo) was letter-writing shorthand for last month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ult.'
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a hardliner.

clue.text: Bolt or rod turned to bearing

indicators.note: turned means the word for rod is read the other way round

parts.note: a pole is a rod
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A mechanic fixes a bolt or a rod on to a bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a piece of hardware but means run off; 'turned' makes ELOP from POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry, so to make a bolt for it.

clue.text: Dramatist as mere relic of Restoration

indicators.note: a restoration rebuilds a ruin, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright as a mere leftover from the Restoration period.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmer Rice was an American playwright (Street Scene). 'Restoration' looks like the period of English drama but rearranges MERE RELIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer Rice was a twentieth-century American playwright.

clue.text: Tank bound to Campbell's Highlands

definitions.meaning: the head of the Clan Campbell in the Scottish Highlands holds a clan leader's title

explanation.surface: A tank is bound for the Highlands where the Campbells live.
explanation.walkthrough: The Campbells are a Scottish Highland clan; each clan has a hereditary head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chieftain was a British army tank, and a clan's head in the Highlands is likewise a chief.

clue.text: First condition of being on trial presumably ?

definitions.text: First condition of being on trial presumably ?

parts.words: First condition of being on trial presumably ?
parts.note: an accused is presumed guiltless until proven otherwise, and so is everyone at birth, before any wrongdoing

explanation.definitionFit: Guiltlessness is the state presumed of a defendant, and the state of a new soul before sin.

clue.text: Time always for the lotos-eaters, it seemed

definitions.text: Time always for the lotos-eaters, it seemed

parts.words: Time always for the lotos-eaters, it seemed
parts.note: a reference to Tennyson's poem, where the mariners came to a land in which it seemed always the same time of day

explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's The Lotos-Eaters: 'In the afternoon they came unto a land / In which it seemed always afternoon.'
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day after midday, which in Tennyson's poem never ended for the lotos-eaters.

clue.text: Crafty chap to enlarge Norma's output right away

parts.note: to enlarge, in an old sense, is to set free or release

indicators.note: output suggests the letters being worked over and produced afresh in a new order
right away tells us R, for right, is taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written, with the S

explanation.surface: A cunning man aims to boost the production of Norma, at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes R from NORMAS, leaving NOMAS, which 'output' rearranges. Freemasons call their movement the Craft, so 'Crafty' is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the masonic brotherhood call their order 'the Craft', so a member is a crafty man.

clue.text: Porcelain identified by Rose for instance'

definitions.text: Porcelain identified by Rose for instance'

parts.words: Porcelain identified by Rose for instance'
parts.note: Chinese porcelain is grouped by its dominant colour, French terms such as rose or verte naming each group

explanation.definitionFit: Famille rose and famille verte are classes of Chinese porcelain named for their colour palette.

clue.text: Set of teeth on which Paul is' said to be engaged

definitions.text: Set of teeth on which Paul is' said to be engaged

parts.words: Set of teeth on which Paul is' said to be engaged
parts.note: the 'teeth' are a toothed bar or wheel, and the name Paul sounds like pawl, the catch that engages those teeth

explanation.definitionFit: A ratch is a ratchet, a toothed bar engaged by a pawl to permit motion one way only.

clue.text: He works doggedly with force

parts.note: 'doggedly' is literal: someone who trains and controls a dog, for instance in the police force

explanation.definitionFit: A dog trainer, especially in the police, controls and works with the animal.

clue.text: He's. not still an active player

definitions.text: He's. not still an active player

parts.words: He's. not still an active player
parts.note: read as someone retired, it really means a person who is never at rest, a doer in some enterprise

explanation.definitionFit: Someone always in motion, as in 'movers and shakers', is neither still nor idle.

clue.text: Girl played with flower

definitions.meaning: A girl's name, as in Twelfth Night
a stringed instrument that is played

explanation.surface: A girl toyed with a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, a stringed instrument larger than a violin, and a pansy-like plant all share this word.

clue.text: Sweetstuff for tea swallowed by routed Incas

indicators.note: being swallowed by means going inside the other letters
routed armies are scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: char is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Defeated Incas are given sugar for their tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'routed' turns INCAS into SACIN, and 'swallowed by' puts CHAR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sweetener used in place of sugar.

clue.text: Prophets of weight in India

definitions.meaning: a seer is an Indian unit of weight, about two pounds

explanation.surface: Prophets of some influence in India.
explanation.walkthrough: A seer was a traditional Indian unit of weight, roughly a kilogram.
explanation.definitionFit: Visionaries who foretell events share their name with an old Indian measure of weight.

clue.text: Tea's hot-stir it up hurry !

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: stirring the tea mixes it, so its letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S

explanation.surface: Tea's hot, give it a stir, quickly!
explanation.definitionFit: Haste means speed or hurry.

clue.text: He's not keen to make trouble in Caledonia

indicators.note: to make trouble in something is to stir it up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A reluctant man is causing a fuss in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland. 'trouble' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laodicean is lukewarm or half-hearted, after the church at Laodicea rebuked in Revelation.

clue.text: Reel shows flying stunts in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the word for the stunts is read backwards

parts.note: loops are aerobatic stunts

explanation.surface: Film footage shows aerobatics run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a reel on which thread, film or tape is wound.

clue.text: Works of art to which LSE perhaps holds title

indicators.note: holds means the other letters go round this one
perhaps suggests these letters may appear in a different order

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: Paintings to whose ownership the London School of Economics lays claim.
explanation.walkthrough: LSE is the London School of Economics; 'perhaps' turns it into ELS, which 'holds' NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels are decorative objects made by fusing glass to metal, so artworks.

clue.text: Late queen crossed to the abbey

definitions.text: Late queen crossed to the abbey

parts.words: Late queen crossed to the abbey
parts.note: Edward I raised a cross at each night's resting place as his dead wife's body was carried to Westminster Abbey

explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Castile, queen of Edward I, is commemorated by the crosses along her funeral route to Westminster.
